newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian markets end mixed while they wait for news.
newsitem.headline: Asian markets end mixed while they wait for news.

text.p: Asian markets generally ended mixed on Wednesday after playing a waiting game.

In Tokyo, the market waited for September futures and options to be settled. In Hong Kong, the Hang Seng waited for corporate results from one of the territory's premier landlords. And in Manila and Kuala Lumpur, they waited for word on U.S. interest rate hikes.
In Bangkok, however, the wait was over as shares halted a nine-day slide after a private fund moved to prop up the market.
Tokyo stocks rebounded by the close after trading lower for most of the day, with the market capped by profit-taking.
Most participants were reluctant to move actively before the Nikkei's September futures and options are settled on Friday, brokers said.
The key 225-share Nikkei average closed up 11.45 points, or 0.06 percent, at 20,571.04, after slipping to 20,425.44.

Hong Kong stocks ended with small gains after investors spent a cautious session searching for direction and awaiting fiscal 1996 earnings from the Henderson group due out after the market closed, analysts said.
The Hang Seng index closed with a gain of 12.74 points, or 0.11 percent, at 11,236.36.
Manila shares finished lower as investors continued to hold back on fears of a U.S. rate hike, brokers said.

"We were not able to sustain Tuesday's momentum. There is still the U.S. rate hike cloud. Everybody's being selective and foreigners cannot move," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities.
The main index closed down 15.61 points, or 0.49 percent, at 3,186.19.
Interest-rate worries also dampened Kuala Lumpur sentiment. The benchmark Composite Index closed down 1.81 points, or 0.16 percent, at 1109.94.
In the day's major turnaround, Thai stocks ended a nine day decline with the index rising 1.44 percent after a private rescue fund entered the market and bought blue chip shares, brokers said.
"The key index could have fallen again today without buying from the rescue fund," said a local broker.
The SET index, which broke through the key psychological 1,000-point level around midday to hit an intra-day high of 1.001.12 points, retreated later and ended up 14.13 points at 996.16.
Singapore shares ended mixed amid a flurry of activity in Indonesian-linked counters, dealers said. The key Straits Times Industrials Index ended 8.72 points, or 0.41 percent, down at 2,102.96.
Taiwan shares closed higher on news that regulators on Tuesday had approved a record one-day influx of US$997 million in foreign investment capital, brokers said.
The index ended up 39.68 points or 0.62 percent at 6,455.44, off a 6,495.42 high.
Seoul stocks closed a fraction lower after investors' hopes that the market would be boosted by improved U.S. semiconductor data fizzled out, brokers said.
The composite stock index lost 1.59 points or 0.20 percent to provisionally close at 801.45.
Jakarta share prices closed sharply lower due to local-led profit-taking in late trading, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index fell 2.39 points, or 0.44 percent, to 541.77 points after touching a low of 540.98 points.

Australian shares closed weaker, the market weighed down by selling of major mining issues as resource sentiment sagged on negative comments about the outlook for steel and copper prices from BHP managing director John Prescott on Tuesday.
The All Ordinaries index finished 9.6 points, or 0.43 percent, lower at 2,246.3.
The New Zealand bourse closed lower, thanks mainly to an eight-cent slide in market heavyweight Telecom. The NZSE-40 capital index closed 8.37 points, or 0.37 percent, lower at 2,235.25.

The dollar was stuck in extremely narrow ranges throughout Tokyo trade, failing to pierce a key psychological point of 110 yen in the face of Japanese exporter and profit-taking offers, dealers said. The dollar had risen as high as 109.95 yen by late Tokyo.

SIMEX Brent futures for October traded above $23.00 per barrel late, increasing on a draw down in U.S. stocks. October last traded at $23.04 per barrel, up 16 cents from London's settlement on Tuesday of $22.88.
Hong Kong bullion ended at US$383.10/60 an ounce against New York's US$383.00/40 close on Tuesday.
